object: German-born British physicist who gave quantum mechanics its probabilistic interpretation — the Born rule, which says the square of the wave function gives the probability of finding a particle. Nobel Prize 1954. Co-developed matrix mechanics with Heisenberg and Jordan at Göttingen. His interpretation was the central idea Einstein objected to at Solvay.
